reading.rtitle: Lunch Fast, Dinner Slow: Eating Out on a Business Trip to the U.S.
paras: In New York, lunch is fast. Many professionals grab a bite at a deli or a food truck and eat at their desk. If a colleague invites you to lunch, expect forty-five minutes, not two hours. At lunchtime, most restaurants accept walk-ins, and you can usually get a booth or a seat at the counter without a reservation.

Dinner is different. A business dinner is where relationships are built, so it is slower and more formal. The dress code is usually business casual. Many restaurants serve small plates to share, and the person who invites you normally pays: in the U.S., the host treats the guests and then expenses the meal to the company. If you want to bring your own bottle of wine, ask about the corkage fee first. And if you are a picky eater, look at the menu online before you go.

Last spring, a Brazilian sales director, Renata, had her first business dinner in Chicago. Before the dinner, her American colleague told her to arrive on time, and he asked her not to talk about prices at the table. At the restaurant, the host asked her to choose the wine. At the end of the night, he asked everyone to raise their glasses, and then he told Renata to make a toast. "I was nervous," she remembers, "but I did it, in English, and the next week we signed the contract."
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- B1 reading, written for this lesson in the style of a business travel magazine

listenings.text: Hi, this message is for Ms. Ito. This is Daniel from the Harbor Grill, calling about your reservation for six people on Thursday at seven thirty. I'm sorry, but our private room is not available that night, so we have a large booth by the window for your group. Our chef asked me to tell you that the kitchen can prepare a menu of small plates to share, and that he can make vegetarian dishes for your guests. Our dress code is business casual, so please ask your guests not to wear shorts or sneakers. If you want to bring your own wine, the corkage fee is thirty dollars per bottle. Please call us back before Wednesday to confirm. Thank you, and have a great day.

Last month, I took a client from Japan to dinner in New York, and I learned a lot. Before we went, my boss told me to choose a quiet place, and she asked me not to order too much food. My client is a picky eater, so I sent him the menu the day before, and I asked him to tell me what he didn't eat. At the restaurant, the waiter asked us to wait ten minutes at the bar, because our table wasn't ready. That was fine, we talked about his family. At the end, my client asked me to let him pay, but I told him that it was my treat. The next morning, I expensed the dinner, and my boss told me to do it again next time. The dinner cost three hundred dollars, and the contract was worth three million.

extra_audio.text: First, I book a table and ask the restaurant about the dress code. Then, I send the menu to my guests and ask them to tell me what they don't eat. Next, at the restaurant, I order some small plates for the table to share. After that, I make a toast to our partnership. Finally, I pay the bill, keep the receipt, and expense the dinner.
